stem: A video-transcoding startup's operations team runs a nightly batch job that must run for up to 40 minutes per invocation, with no EC2 instances to patch or scale.

choices.text: AWS Lambda, with the function's timeout raised to 40 minutes
AWS Lambda with provisioned concurrency enabled to keep the function warm for the full 40 minutes
An EC2 Spot Fleet that the team patches and scales itself
AWS Fargate, running the transcoding job as a container with no EC2 instances to manage

rationale: AWS Fargate runs a container with a specified CPU and memory for as long as the job needs, without the team provisioning or patching any underlying EC2 instances, which fits a 40-minute batch job with no servers to manage. A Lambda function has a hard maximum execution timeout of 900 seconds (15 minutes) per invocation, so a 40-minute timeout cannot be configured at all. Provisioned concurrency only keeps a function's execution environment warm to reduce cold starts; it does not raise the 15-minute hard ceiling, so the same 40-minute job still cannot run to completion. An EC2 Spot Fleet could run the job for 40 minutes, but the team would be back to patching and scaling instances itself, which the requirement explicitly rules out.
